description: Help parents quickly choose consistent, household-friendly merchant names by suggesting existing effective merchant names while they type in the transaction display-name editor. Suggestions should reduce retyping and drift without introducing fuzzy matching, schema churn, or automatic normalization behavior.

timing.gatingCondition: Feature 22 transaction identity overrides is merged because the suggestion UI builds directly on the display-name edit surface.

principles: Suggestions assist naming; they do not replace deliberate parent choice
Selecting a suggestion fills the edit field only and does not silently create a future rename rule
Suggestion source data comes from existing household transaction history, not external normalization services
V1 uses prefix search only; no fuzzy matching or spelling correction
Suggestions rank likely household conventions ahead of rare one-offs using frequency and recency
Parent-only editing remains intact; kid surfaces stay read-only
SECRETS INVARIANT: suggestion responses expose only displayable merchant text already visible in Family Pulse transaction history

techStack.database: PostgreSQL query over existing transactions using effective display name projection
techStack.integrationPoints: Transaction detail overlays on dashboard and transactions page, plus a small suggestions API
techStack.testing: node:test for suggestion ranking/query behavior and Playwright for keyboard/mouse suggestion selection in the display-name editor

executionStatus.mode: Seed stories with passes false and update during implementation.

userStories.title: Parent sees existing merchant suggestions while typing
acceptanceCriteria: When a parent types into the display-name input in transaction detail, Family Pulse requests suggestions after a short debounce once at least 2 characters are present
Suggestions are built from existing effective merchant names already stored in Family Pulse transaction history
The suggestion list is hidden for kids and hidden when the input is empty or below the minimum prefix length
The API and UI return at most a small fixed number of suggestions suitable for an inline dropdown
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for API query shape and auth; Playwright for dropdown visibility and debounce-driven suggestions.

userStories.title: Suggestions rank consistent household names first
acceptanceCriteria: Prefix matches are returned only when the suggestion text starts with the typed prefix, case-insensitive
Suggestions are ranked by a pragmatic combination of frequency and recency so the household's common naming convention tends to appear first
Duplicate suggestion labels are collapsed so the dropdown does not show the same cleaned merchant name repeatedly
The current transaction's already-selected effective display name may appear, but duplicates are removed from the final list
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for prefix filtering, deduplication, and ordering logic.

userStories.title: Selecting a suggestion is assistive only
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking or keyboard-selecting a suggestion fills the display-name input with that merchant name
Choosing a suggestion does not itself save the transaction or create/update a future rename rule
The parent must still explicitly click Save Name to persist the transaction-level override
The apply-to-future checkbox state remains under explicit parent control after a suggestion is chosen
userStories.testStrategy: Playwright coverage for click and keyboard selection, plus confirmation that save is still explicit.

userStories.title: Suggestion UI stays lightweight and non-disruptive
acceptanceCriteria: The dropdown appears directly under the display-name input and dismisses on blur, Escape, or suggestion selection
The existing transaction detail overlay behavior remains intact, including Save/Clear actions and note/attachment interactions
The suggestion UI works on both dashboard and transactions-page detail overlays without introducing a separate page-level merchant editor
userStories.testStrategy: Playwright for visibility/dismissal behavior on both parent entry points plus targeted regression checks.

medium: Naive prefix queries could drift toward a full-table scan if the transaction table grows. Mitigation: keep the result cap low, minimum query length above 1 character, and start with a simple indexed/coalesced query.
low: Suggestions may reinforce slightly inconsistent household naming if past data is messy. Mitigation: rank by frequency/recency and keep selection optional.
Autocomplete UI can feel noisy if shown too early. Mitigation: debounce requests and require a minimum typed prefix.
operational: If merchant naming later gets a dedicated dictionary, this API should be able to switch sources behind the same UI contract.

preFlightChecklist: Confirm whether the minimum prefix length should be 2 or 3 characters; default to 2 for responsiveness
Choose a fixed suggestion cap, likely 5 to 8
Inspect the current display-name save flow so suggestion dropdown state does not interfere with existing Escape/overlay behavior
Decide whether frequency, recency, or a blended score should dominate ranking in v1
